sources.title: Deepseek: The Quiet Giant Leading China's AI Race
sources.quote_checked: We will not change to closed source. We believe having a strong technical ecosystem first is more important. | In the face of disruptive technologies, moats created by closed source are temporary. | Open source, publishing papers, in fact, do not cost us anything. | We are mostly fresh graduates from top universities, PhD candidates in their fourth or fifth year, and some young people who graduated just a few years ago. | Our hiring standard has always been passion and curiosity. | What we see is that Chinese AI can't be in the position of following forever. | Money has never been the problem for us; bans on shipments of advanced chips are the problem. | More investments do not equal more innovation. | we don't subsidize nor make exorbitant profits. | Our ultimate goal is still to achieve AGI.

sources.title: Who is Liang Wenfeng, the founder of Chinese AI startup DeepSeek?
sources.quote_checked: It is like buying a piano. | only emphasized making money and ignored innovation.

sources.title: The Deep Roots of DeepSeek: How It All Began
sources.by: Yu Lili (36Kr), translated and republished by Tony Peng
sources.quote_checked: Many might think there's an undisclosed business logic behind this, but in reality, it's primarily driven by curiosity. | For researchers, the thirst for computational power is insatiable. | Our goal is clear: not to focus on verticals and applications, but on research and exploration. | Innovation often arises spontaneously, not through deliberate arrangement, nor can it be taught. | But in the long run, experience is less important; foundational abilities, creativity, and passion are more crucial. | A principle at High-Flyer is to look at ability, not experience.

sources.title: Founder says DeepSeek prioritises AGI over profit, likely to keep top models open-source, Yicai reports
